I stand between the centuries, the baton a needle stitching time,

The raw, unbridled air before the machine took hold.

[Music shifts to a solo wooden flute, airy and breathy]
Consider the woodwind—the ancient, hollow reed.

Bound by the reach of a human finger.
Its scale was a fragile thing, bending to the natural harmonic,
Rich in breath, haunting in its imperfection.

We lost the idiosyncratic breath to gain the infinite scale.
Yet, as I raise my arm, I realize the wind remains the same,

Use a finger-picking rhythmic feel, a slow tempo, and a narrative structure consisting of long, descriptive verses.","genre":"Folk","subgenre":"Dark Folk","mood":"Eerie, Mysterious","theme":"Pact with Forest Spirit","language":"English","perspective":"First Person","song_structure":"Verse-Verse-Verse-Verse-Outro","rhyme_scheme":"AABB","tempo_feel":"Slow, Finger-picking","complexity":"Medium","lyrics":"The path dissolved beneath my boots of worn and weary leather,

I counted time in shadows cast instead of passing hours.
I heard a whisper in the bark, a sigh within the pine,

And felt the cold of winter deep begin to grow in me.
